newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov., lawmakers near budget deal - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov., lawmakers near budget deal - report.

text.p: Connecticut Republican Gov. John Rowland and the Democrat-controlled legislature are nearing an agreement on the state budget, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
"I still contend that we can have a sizable income tax cut this year," Rowland was quoted as saying.
Democrats, however, have been pushing a cut in the property tax.
Rowland said he was open to a property tax cut, possibly similar to the $100 credit approved two years ago for taxes paid on houses, condominiums or automobiles.

The governor has proposed cutting the gasoline tax by five cents per gallon on July 1, but he now says he would not oppose a plan by Senate Democrats to cut three cents per gallon in the first year and two cents in the second year of the two-year budget, the Courant said.
Before any taxes can be cut, legislators must first balance the two-year, $20 billion budget.
Rowland said that he and the Democrats are about $300 million apart, but said the two sides were basically "95 percent" in agreement overall.
This year's legislative session ends on June 4.
